location: Laguna Miscanti, Los Flamencos National Reserve, Antofagasta Region
alt: Blue altiplanic lagoon of Miscanti beneath Andean volcanic peaks and dry grassland at over 4,000 m
caption: Laguna Miscanti, around 4,140 m in Los Flamencos National Reserve, seen from the altiplano road. Day 5 is the highest, longest drive of the trip: Miscanti and Miñiques are reached only after several nights of acclimatisation, with vicuñas and volcano cones around the shore.

commonsFile: File:Géiseres del Tatio, Atacama, Chile, 2016-02-01, DD 01-02 HDR.JPG
location: El Tatio geyser field, Antofagasta Region
alt: Steaming vents and mineral-crusted pools of the El Tatio geyser field in the high Andes
caption: Steam and mineral-crusted vents at the El Tatio geyser field, about 4,300 m up. Day 7 starts here before sunrise, when sub-zero air makes the plumes most visible; the 90 km drive from San Pedro is done in the dark.

commonsFile: File:Anfiteatro, Valle de la Luna, San Pedro de Atacama, Chile, 2016-02-01, DD 153.JPG
location: Valle de la Luna, Cordillera de la Sal, near San Pedro de Atacama
alt: Eroded salt and clay ridges of the Anfiteatro in Valle de la Luna
caption: The Anfiteatro, a bowl of eroded salt and clay ridges in the Valle de la Luna, Cordillera de la Sal. Day 6 visits it at low altitude, a gentler day between the high-plateau outings; sunset light gives the ridges their colour.

commonsFile: File:FLAMINGO LAGUNA CHAXA SAN PEDRO DE ATACAMA 3.jpg
alt: Pink flamingos wading in the shallow brine of Laguna Chaxa on the Salar de Atacama, with salt crust in the foreground
caption: Flamingos feeding in the shallow brine of Laguna Chaxa on the Salar de Atacama, about 2,300 m. Day 4 begins here at dawn, when the birds are most active, before an evening astronomy tour.

location: Piedras Rojas, Salar de Aguas Calientes, Antofagasta Region
alt: Red volcanic rocks and a turquoise salt lagoon at Piedras Rojas on the altiplano
caption: Red volcanic rocks beside a turquoise salt lagoon at Piedras Rojas, on the high road from Socaire. The second stop of day 5, a colour contrast to Miscanti, reached by a track that must be checked for conditions before leaving San Pedro.

alt: White-washed adobe church of San Francisco in Chiu Chiu at sunset with a cactus-wood roof and bell gable
caption: The 17th-century adobe church of San Francisco in Chiu Chiu, with a cactus-wood roof and white-washed walls. Day 8 pairs it with the Chuquicamata copper pit, linking Atacameño heritage to the industrial landscape of the Calama region.

location: Chajnantor plateau, near San Pedro de Atacama
alt: Milky Way arching over white radio antennas of the ALMA observatory on the Chajnantor plateau at night
caption: The Milky Way above radio antennas of the ALMA observatory on the Chajnantor plateau, near San Pedro de Atacama. It illustrates the dry, high-altitude sky that the group will seek on a moonless night near the 8 March new moon, on an astronomy tour booked from the oasis.

location: Catedrales de Tara, Salar de Tara
alt: Wind-carved volcanic rock towers known as the Cathedrals of Tara on the high plateau
caption: Wind-carved volcanic rock towers known as the Catedrales de Tara, at the edge of the Salar de Tara. A highlight of day 10, the remote border-plateau excursion where local guidance on tracks and weather matters most.

commonsFile: File:Arch of the Pukará de Quitor fortress framing the Licancabur volcano (potw2501a).jpg
location: Pukará de Quitor, near San Pedro de Atacama
alt: A stone arch of the Pukará de Quitor fortress framing the cone of Licancabur volcano
caption: A stone arch of the Pukará de Quitor, a pre-Hispanic hillside fortress, framing Licancabur volcano above San Pedro. Day 3 is an easy acclimatisation walk here and in the local museum, setting the Atacameño context for the rest of the trip.

alt: Stone and adobe houses of the Atacameño village of Caspana clustered along a green ravine
caption: Stone and adobe houses of Caspana, an Atacameño village in a green ravine fed by a stream. The overnight stop on day 7 after El Tatio, a community-run homestay in a village with its own heritage museum.

commonsFile: File:Iglesia de San Lucas, Toconao, Chile, 2016-02-06, DD 33.JPG
alt: White volcanic-stone church of San Lucas in Toconao with its separate bell tower under a clear blue sky
caption: The church of San Lucas and its separate bell tower in Toconao, an oasis village built of white liparite stone south of San Pedro. It is the lunch and fuel stop on the road to the Miscanti lagoons and gives a first look at Atacameño village architecture.

commonsFile: File:Monjes de la Pacana, Chile, 2016-02-07, DD 03.JPG
location: Monjes de la Pacana, Antofagasta Region
alt: Tall wind-sculpted volcanic rock pillars of the Monjes de la Pacana rising from the high desert plateau
caption: The Monjes de la Pacana, a field of tall volcanic rock pillars on the plateau beyond Salar de Tara. Day 10 ends here, in the most remote landscape of the itinerary, where tracks and weather decide how far the group goes.
